10.1002_adfm.78750: Fast‐charging and long‐life energy storage systems require electrode architectures that can sustain rapid ion transport while resisting structural and interfacial degradation. Dual‐ion batteries are attractive high‐voltage systems based on reversible anion intercalation into a graphite cathode. However, their long‐term operation is limited by large graphite volume changes, solvent co‐intercalation, unstable cathode‐electrolyte interphase formation, and electrolyte decomposition at high potentials. This study demonstrates that the spatial location of an atomic layer deposition (ALD) coating is a decisive factor in stabilizing graphite cathodes. After identifying ZrO 2 as an effective coating, electrode‐level ALD and particle‐level ALD were compared using the same coating chemistry. Unlike electrode‐level ALD, which coats the pre‐fabricated composite electrode and covers inactive components, particle‐level ALD directly modifies graphite particles before electrode fabrication. This particle‐level ZrO 2 coating improves electrode cohesion, preserves electronic connectivity, enriches PF 6 − near the graphite interface, and facilitates anion transport. As a result, the particle‐level ALD graphite cathode delivers stable high‐rate cycling for 4000 cycles at a 5 C‐rate. Post‐cycling analyses confirm that particle‐level ZrO 2 reinforces graphite, suppresses solvent‐assisted structural collapse, and mitigates excessive electrolyte decomposition. This work establishes the scale of coating application, particle‐level versus electrode‐level, as a key design principle for durable graphite cathodes in fast‐cycling dual‐ion batteries.
10.1002_adsc.70759: 1,2,5‐Thiadiazines, a class of six‐membered heterocycles containing two nitrogen atoms and one sulfur atom, have been widely incorporated into various biologically active molecules. Herein, we report a green and efficient electrochemical three‐component reaction of isonitriles, elemental sulfur, and diamines to access 1,2,5‐thiadiazines under mild conditions. Elemental sulfur serves as an inexpensive, readily available, stable, and nontoxic sulfur source. Both aliphatic and aryl isonitriles are suitable substrates for this strategy at room temperature, and a series of 1,2,5‐thiadiazines are prepared with up to 77% yields. In this one‐pot transformation, one C─N bond, one C─S bond, and one S─N bond are constructed with high regioselectivity, demonstrating excellent functional group tolerance and high atom economy.
10.1002_cey2.70320: The electrochemical nitrate reduction reaction (NO 3 − RR) offers an attractive route for removing NO 3 − pollution and sustainably producing ammonia (NH 3 ). Rational regulation of *H species supply and key intermediates adsorption is critical for enhancing NO 3 − RR performance. Herein, we design a heterostructured CoNi/MoN catalyst, where MoN nanosheets are decorated with CoNi nanoparticles, to optimize the interfacial water structure and intermediates adsorption. This heterostructured catalyst exhibits a high NH 3 Faradaic efficiency of 96.8% and an attractive NH 3 yield rate of 22.3 mg h −1 cm −2 , outperforming most of the reported electrocatalysts under same NO 3 − concentration. Furthermore, using CoNi/MoN/NF as both the anode and cathode, a two‐electrode system coupling NO 3 − RR with 5‐hydroxymethylfurfural oxidation reaction achieves highly effective co‐production of NH 3 and 2,5‐furandicarboxylic acid. Experimental and theoretical calculation results reveal that the strong metal‐support interaction between CoNi nanoparticles and MoN nanosheets induces electron transfer from CoNi species to MoN nanosheets. The electron‐enriched MoN sites at the CoNi/MoN interface can efficiently capture K + to form K + ‐hydrated water (K + ‐H 2 O), which facilitates H 2 O dissociation to generate *H for accelerating the hydrogenation steps of NO 3 − RR. Meanwhile, the electron‐deficient CoNi nanoparticles with the upshifted d‐band center enhance NO 3 − adsorption and reduce the free energy barrier of NO 3 − RR.
10.1002_smll.74329: Lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs) have become the leading energy storage systems for both portable electronic devices and stationary energy storage applications. However, their further advancement is hindered by the lack of fast‐charging, durable anode materials. Metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as promising candidate anode materials owing to their high porosity and diverse structures. This study developed a novel LIB anode Bi/C@C featuring a distinctive core‐shell structure via a metal‐organic framework (MOF)‐derived approach, exhibiting rapid lithium storage performance (275 mAh g −1 at 5000 mA g −1 ) and exceptional cycling stability (85% capacity retention over 2000 cycles). This structure contains a 3D Bi‐C porous core and a dense yet defect‐rich carbon shell, enabling efficient ion/charge transport, functional interfacial isolation, and mechanical buffering against volume changes. DFT calculations further demonstrate that the core‐shell structure possesses strong lithium‐ion adsorption and a low reaction energy barrier (‐0.32 eV), effectively facilitating electrochemical kinetics. Furthermore, the Bi/C@C‐500//LiNi 0.5 Co 0.2 Mn 0.3 O 2 full cell demonstrates unparalleled rate capacity (183 mAh g −1 at 20 C) and remarkable cycling stability (86% capacity retention after 100 cycles). These findings establish the 3D porous core‐shell Bi/C@C as a highly promising anode for LIBs, holding great significance for advancing the development of high‐performance energy storage technologies.
10.1002_smll.76312: The electrocatalytic NO 3 − reduction reaction (eNO 3 RR) is a facile and green method for the generation of electricity with the simultaneous production of NH 3 . Herein, we report the synthesis of hierarchical nickel–cobalt–copper borate ((Ni 1/3 Co 1/3 Cu 1/3 ) 3 B 2 O 6 ) nanosheets via a carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) laser irradiation method and investigate their eNO 3 RR performance in a 1 m KOH electrolyte containing 0.1 m KNO 3 . Initially, (Ni 1/3 Co 1/3 Cu 1/3 ) 3 B 2 O 6 is synthesized via CO 2 laser irradiation within a short processing period of 1 min, where this method enables a rapid material synthesis compared with conventional methods, such as hydrothermal, solvothermal, and wet‐chemical approaches. The (Ni 1/3 Co 1/3 Cu 1/3 ) 3 B 2 O 6 catalyst achieves a maximum NH 3 yield rate of 4.1 mg h −1 cm −2 and a Faradaic efficiency of 90.69% at −0.3 V vs. the reversible hydrogen electrode. In‐depth analysis of eNO 3 RR kinetics using in situ Raman, ex situ X‐ray diffraction, and ex situ Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy reveals information on the reaction intermediates and reaction pathways involved. Extended density functional theory calculations further corroborate the experimental findings related to reaction intermediates and pathways during the eNO 3 RR. A zinc (Zn)–NO 3 − battery assembled using (Ni 1/3 Co 1/3 Cu 1/3 ) 3 B 2 O 6 as the cathode and a Zn plate as the anode exhibits an open‐circuit voltage of 1.44 V at 12 mA cm −2 .
10.1016_j.memsci.2025.124884: Concentration polarization (CP) is determined by neutron transmission in a reverse osmosis (RO) system consisting of two cells, one with and the other without an RO membrane, to get the net neutron response for the feed solution in front and far from the membrane separately. The aqueous feed was a dilute solution of NaCl and GdCl 3 . The special feature of these experiments is that GdCl 3 can be selectively determined with neutrons, since the neutron absorption cross-section of Gd is larger orders of magnitude compared to other elements such as Na, Cl, and water, and therefore has a strong influence on the overall transparency of the sample for neutrons. It is therefore the transmission of neutrons through both cells (one with and the other without membrane), by which the concentration and CP of GdCl 3 can be determined. Transmission and small-angle scattering (SANS) were measured in parallel, demonstrating the performance of this method as an in-situ method for determining CP as a function of time under near-realistic conditions. The neutron experiments are complemented by measurements of permeate flux and electrical conductivity of the feed, which were used to determine the salt concentrations, the osmotic pressure and the concentration polarization of the two salts individually and of a mixture of both. The CP results of this study are in good agreement with the values presented in the literature, determined mainly from flux data under a wide variety of conditions. • Operando reverse osmosis. • Neutron transmission to determine GdCl 3 concentration. • Permeate flux. • Concentration polarization of GdCl 3 and NaCl.
10.1016_j.memsci.2026.126119: Efficiently recovering lithium from complex battery waste leachates is still a major challenge due to the dilution of lithium and the presence of competing multivalent ions. This study proposes a selective upcycling strategy in which the leachate from battery waste is utilised both as a direct precursor for material synthesis as well as the feedstock for separation. Cu-based metal-organic framework (MOF) was synthesised from multi-ion leachates and then incorporated into a thin-film nanocomposite (TFN) membrane that enables the selective recovery of lithium. This significantly enhances the membrane's hydrophilicity and tailors transport pathways, enabling synergistic pore sieving and ion-selective transport. The optimised MOF-TFN membrane exhibits high Li + /Cu 2+ selectivity (up to 16.0), with the Li + :Cu 2+ ratio increasing from 2.4:1 in the feed to 46.1:1 in the permeate, in multiple filtration cycles. A lithium recovery rate of 99.8% was achieved over six consecutive filtration cycles while maintaining a high Cu 2+ rejection rate of 94.8%. Additionally, the membrane demonstrates stable transport performance, with a water flux of 110.35 LMH at 7.5 bar, as well as pressure-independent permeability, indicating structural robustness. The membrane also exhibits excellent antifouling properties, with flux recovery ratios (FRR) ranging from 92.8% to 86.5%. This is supported by reversible fouling behaviour and effective surface regeneration. This work presents a sustainable, integrated approach to lithium recovery that bridges waste valorisation and membrane separation within a single circular framework: battery waste-MOF-membrane-lithium recovery. This offers a promising pathway for the practical recycling of resources in complex, multi-ion systems.
10.1021_acsami.6c16482: Oil pollution from petroleum-related activities and oily industrial wastewater pose a persistent challenge to aquatic environments, motivating the development of efficient sorbent and separation materials. However, conventional aerogels usually require multistep fabrication and show limited mechanical robustness. Herein, a silanized topo-vascular cellulose aerogel (STVCA) is developed through a top-down strategy using the oriented transport architecture of Spatholobus suberectus Dunn stems as a structural template. Vapor-phase silanization tailors the cellulose interface while the processed scaffold retains key topological features of the native hierarchical vascular architecture, combining low-surface-energy chemistry with the inherited channel organization and mechanical integrity. The resulting STVCA serves as a robust, fast mass-transfer medium for oil/water separation, showing rapid oil wetting, stable hydrophobicity, and anisotropic capillary transport. Dry STVCA reaches a compressive stress of 28.41 MPa at 80% radial strain (σ80), whereas oil-loaded STVCA reaches σ80 = 27.14 MPa and retains 91% of its initial σ80 after 80 compression cycles. The cross-sectional surface and longitudinal faces have mean static water contact angles of 151.05 ± 4.01° and 143.80 ± 5.92°, while a representative internal cut-surface measurement reaches 155.7°. Owing to the preserved vascular-bundle topology, STVCA achieves anisotropic mass transfer, a chloroform uptake capacity of 11.73 ± 0.61 g·g-1, a continuous separation flux of 13126 L·m-2·h-1, and a separation efficiency of up to 99%. This biomass-derived aerogel provides a durable platform for oil-spill remediation.
10.1021_acscatal.5c09108: The application of room-temperature sodium-sulfur (RT Na-S) batteries is severely hindered by two major roadblocks, namely, the shuttle effect of sodium polysulfides (NaPSs) and the slow kinetics of the sulfur reduction reaction (SRR). To resolve these issues, in this study, bifunctional single-atom catalysts (SACs) designed by anchoring transition metal (TM) atoms on 4-5-6-8 member-ringed carbon nanoribbons (CNRs) are proposed. The introduction of TM atoms tunes the binding strength of NaPSs to effectively suppress the shuttle effect. Gibbs’s free energy calculations reveal that TM-CNRs substantially improve the kinetics of the SRR by reducing the rate-determining energy barrier. For some of the TM-CNRs, the reduction can be as large as 97%. Based on the binding strength of NaPSs and the rate-determining activation barrier, SACs are categorized into strong, moderate, and weak cathode hosts. With suppressed sulfur poisoning activity, TM-CNRs reduce the decomposition barrier for Na2S by approximately a factor of three. The gradient boosting regression algorithm-based machine learning model reveals that a combined descriptor, β (ionization energy of TM × number of sulfur atoms in the target NaPS), governs the binding strength of NaPSs. This study, along with providing a fundamental understanding of TM-CNRs' catalytic activity, elucidates the suitability of moderate class TM-CNRs for RT Na-S batteries.
